Time-transformed goodness-of-fit diagnostic

Source: R/gof_time_transform.R
gof_time_transform.Rd

Computes the model-implied cumulative expected count over time, $$\tau(t) = \int_0^t \Lambda(u) \, du,$$ where \(\Lambda(t)\) is the fitted intensity integrated over the study region, and compares it with the observed cumulative event count.

Usage

gof_time_transform(fit, dt = 1, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fit

A fitted object of class semihawkes_fit returned by fit_semihawkes().

dt

Temporal grid spacing, in days, used to approximate the time integral.

level

Coverage level of the pointwise KS-style bands.

Value

An object of class semihawkes_gof_time: a list containing grid, events, bands and level.

Details

Under a correctly specified temporal intensity, the transformed event times are approximately a unit-rate Poisson process. The function also returns pointwise KS-style acceptance bands for the observed cumulative count.

Examples

# \donttest{
# A quick fit to one year of the bundled simulated data: a coarse grid, a
# coarse triggering-kernel grid and two EM iterations keep it to a few
# seconds. Real analyses need finer settings and more iterations.
cache_dir <- tempfile("spHawkes_marks_")
fit <- fit_semihawkes(
  sim_events, sim_region,
  date_col  = "date",
  end_date  = "2022-01-01",
  cell_size = 1000,
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  trigger_spatial_args = list(x_range = 2000, x_step = 250),
  trigger_window_dist  = 2000,
  n_iter  = 2,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed    = 1
)
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
gof <- gof_time_transform(fit, dt = 1)
plot(gof)

# }
